decision: Walk-forward, expanding window, one forecast per quarter at the real forecast date; leave-one-out kept only as an in-sample fit statistic
alternatives_considered: Leave-one-out; k-fold (purged)
reason: LOO and k-fold train on quarters after the one they predict. For a one-step expanding window every training target is already reported at the origin, so nothing needs purging or embargoing (López de Prado's purging applies when training data overlap the test label window)

decision: Origin = the day before Nordic reports quarter t: Logitech and Nordic through t-1, Nordic guidance for t, distributor state through t-1
alternatives_considered: Use every column dated t-1 or earlier as in the panel
reason: Logitech reports about a week after Nordic, so Logitech quarter t is not known; the step-6 regression used the distributor state of quarter t, which Nordic discloses only in the t report (a leak)
evidence: report dates in the case brief (Nordic 22 Oct, Logitech ~27 Oct)
effect: L6 uses state(t-1); L6leak kept only to size the leak

decision: Lags (1-3), ridge alpha and the step-3 lag (2) are fixed from the reasoned prior; each origin only re-estimates coefficients
alternatives_considered: Choose lags / alpha by cross-validation at every origin
reason: Choosing hyper-parameters on the full sample is look-ahead; re-tuning on 8-12 points would be noise
effect: no hyper-parameter sees the test quarter

decision: Benchmark = guidance midpoint x (1 + mean beat of the previous 4 quarters)
alternatives_considered: Regime-conditioned beat (step 7)
reason: Regime labels are dated after the fact; a real-time analyst knows only the recent beats. This is the step-7 method in its real-time form

decision: A lag model is scored as a TILT on guidance: total = guide + (model consumer - guidance-implied consumer)
alternatives_considered: Score the lag model's consumer forecast on its own
reason: That is how the model would enter the forecast; guidance already covers Industrial & Health and the level

decision: Each model's RMSE is compared with the benchmark re-scored on exactly the same quarters
alternatives_considered: Compare full-sample RMSEs
reason: Lag models start later (they need 8 training quarters); the destock quarters they skip were the hard ones for guidance too

decision: Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction (autocovariance to lag h-1) and the encompassing regression (actual - guide) = a + b x tilt with HAC s.e.; with n = 5-14 the results are called 'suggestive' unless p < 0.05
alternatives_considered: Report RMSE only
reason: RMSE differences on 10 quarters can be luck; the encompassing test asks the decision-relevant question: does the model's disagreement with guidance predict the miss?

decision: Also test the quarter after the guided one (h=2) against the last guide carried by last year's seasonal step
alternatives_considered: Only h=1
reason: At h=1 Nordic's guidance embeds its own order book, which already contains Logitech's orders; a lagged Logitech signal can only add information where no guidance exists. Consensus would be the better h=2 benchmark but is paywalled
effect: h=2 is where the lag model earns its place

decision: Latest (restated) data, not first releases
alternatives_considered: Rebuild real-time vintages
reason: First-release vintages are not systematically public for Nordic / Logitech segments; restatements (step 1) make the back-test slightly flattering to the models - stated as a limitation

decision: 8 quarters before the first forecast
reason: 4 regressors + intercept in L6 need at least ~2x as many points; 10 would leave almost no forecasts

decision: h=1: no lag-model tilt on the October point forecasts (the step-7 design already has none). h=2: the step-3 reduced form and the share-weighted step-6 model are the Q4 2026 outlook; where they disagree the outlook is a range, not a point
alternatives_considered: Tilt the Q3 forecasts by the lag model
reason: The walk-forward says a tilt would have cost 4-6x the error at h=1 and saved ~40% at h=2

decision: Model Nordic's guidance MISS (actual / guide midpoint - 1), not revenue growth
alternatives_considered: Regress revenue growth on all factors
reason: Guidance already embeds Nordic's order book (6b: lag models lose to guidance at h=1). Only the miss is information guidance does not have; any factor must be judged on it
evidence: walkforward_metrics_h1.csv (encompassing: no lag model adds to guidance)

topic: factor list and signs fixed first
decision: Four channel factors, signs from economics, lags so every factor is dated t-1 at the forecast date; written in config/model.yaml before the back-test ran; none dropped after seeing results
alternatives_considered: Screen many candidates and keep the ones that work
reason: Selection is the biggest over-fitting risk with 11-18 points. Stated honestly: the four were chosen after step 3 had shown the data, so researcher degrees of freedom remain; the pre-registered live forecast is the clean test
effect: Logitech acceleration kept although its in-sample sign disagrees

decision: C_t = mean(sign_k x expanding z_k,t); model beat = a + b C (2 parameters)
alternatives_considered: OLS / ridge weights on the factors
reason: With ~15 points estimated weights are noise-prone (Dawes 1979; DeMiguel et al. 2009). In this sample ridge happened to do better - equal weights stay primary because they were fixed before the run, ridge is the logged challenger

decision: Each z uses the mean and sd of the factor up to t-1 only
alternatives_considered: Full-sample standardisation
reason: Full-sample mean/sd leaks the future into every z

decision: Placebo with AR(1) noise factors through the identical pipeline (1000 draws); leave-one-factor-out; all distinct sign combinations; estimated-weight challengers; slope stability; OOS R2, Diebold-Mariano, cumulative squared-error gain
alternatives_considered: Report RMSE only
reason: Each test targets one channel of over-fitting: chance, one factor carrying it, sign choice, weights, instability

decision: Step 7 uses the composite only if OOS R2 > 0, placebo p <= 0.10, >= 10 forecasts and >= 3/4 leave-one-out composites beat the benchmark - thresholds written in config before the run and applied by code
alternatives_considered: Decide by eye after the run
reason: A rule fixed in advance cannot be bent to the result

decision: When adopted, drop forecast lines the composite already captures (capacity_worry_pull_in = distributor-state signal) and use the composite's walk-forward RMSE as the beat error instead of historical dispersion + 3 pt extra
alternatives_considered: Keep all adjustments and the old band
reason: The same signal counted twice biases the point; the walk-forward RMSE is the measured out-of-sample error, so the ad-hoc extra is no longer needed

decision: The live forecast (primary and ridge challenger) is appended once per (target, spec hash) to composite_prereg_log.csv and committed; a changed spec gets a new hash and a new row
alternatives_considered: Re-compute the forecast whenever the code changes
reason: After 22 Oct the print scores a forecast that could not be tuned to it; re-specifications stay visible

decision: Build a peer panel (Pipeline D: Microchip, NXP, TI, ADI, onsemi, Silicon Labs; 2011-2026) instead of adding terms to the Nordic model
alternatives_considered: Absolute-value or +/- slope terms; regime switches on Nordic alone
reason: The Nordic composite holds ~2 independent observations (R4); extra terms would be fitted to them. Several cycles and firms are the only way to add independent information

decision: Actual revenue = FIRST-reported XBRL value; guides = the INITIAL guide of each quarter (not mid-quarter updates)
alternatives_considered: Latest restated values; the last Item 2.02 filing per quarter
reason: Restated values and mid-quarter updates measure a different company or use information the guide did not have (Silicon Labs divestiture; TI mid-quarter updates)

topic: traps handled in the peer data
decision: Unit typo corrected with a flag; months->weeks definition break not bridged; M&A / divestiture quarters excluded with reasons; GAAP one-off replaced by the release's comparable figure (quote checked); plausibility band 0.25-4x (0.5-2x dropped a real destock guide)
alternatives_considered: Silent fixes; tight filters
reason: Every correction is a rule a reader can check; a filter that removes the destock extremes is selection bias

decision: beat = firm FE (mean past beat) + b1 own forward DIO + b2 Microchip distributor-days change; same signs as the Nordic composite; walk-forward by quarter; SE clustered by quarter; DM on the cross-sectional average loss per quarter
alternatives_considered: Re-choose factors on the panel
reason: Testing the SAME mechanism on new data is the external test; changing it would re-open the search

decision: Estimate on the peers (12 from 2026-09-26) only; apply to Nordic, which never enters estimation
alternatives_considered: Include Nordic in the pool
reason: Only a model that never saw Nordic can validate the Nordic result

topic: what the panel means for the forecast
decision: Result: the channel factors do not beat each firm's own mean beat out of sample (R5). The adoption gate (B17) was fixed before this evidence existed; whether to keep the composite in the Q3 forecast is put to the analyst rather than changed by code
alternatives_considered: Let code drop the composite automatically
reason: Adding a failed external test to the gate now would be a rule written after seeing a result; the decision belongs to the analyst, with the evidence shown in R5

decision: Revert the Nordic Q3 forecast to the regime-conditioned historical beat; keep the composite as a pre-registered challenger scored after the print
alternatives_considered: Keep the composite in the forecast because its pre-stated gate passed
reason: Independent evidence (peer panel, R5) says the mechanism does not generalise; with weak external evidence the simpler model is the default, and the cost is small (about USD 0.8m on the point, inside the band)
effect: Nordic Q3 point back to the benchmark method; capacity_worry_pull_in line restored

decision: No separate model per cycle phase; phase may enter only as an intercept or through the uncertainty band
alternatives_considered: Fit one model per phase (downturn / upturn)
reason: On the peer panel, with 24 downturn quarters across six firms, phase-specific slopes worsen out-of-sample forecasts (downturns most); on Nordic's single cycle they would be fitted to one observation each

decision: Firm-specific behaviour is modelled by partial pooling (random-effects shrinkage towards the peer slope) and, as a next step, by observable firm characteristics (distribution share, end-market mix, lead times) — not by a free Nordic slope
alternatives_considered: Use Nordic's own slope; or the peer slope unchanged
reason: Nordic's own slope is ~10 between-firm sd from the peers but rests on ~4 independent observations; shrinkage puts 3-14% weight on it

decision: Criterion fixed in config before any candidate's slope was seen: distribution share >= 35% (Nordic 42-55%); candidates listed on business description (consumer / IoT / broad-market semiconductors guiding quarterly in their 8-K); characteristics read from each latest 10-K and quote-checked
alternatives_considered: Pick peers that 'look right' after seeing their slopes
reason: Choosing peers after seeing results would re-open the search; TI (distribution <20%) fails the criterion although it had the highest slope
effect: 11 of 12 fetched peers qualify (TI fails); 4 candidates excluded (share not disclosed)

decision: Recorded with its definition; tried only as an exploratory one-covariate meta-regression, never used for the Nordic prediction
alternatives_considered: Use it as a second meta-regression covariate
reason: Definitions differ by company (Consumer / High-End Consumer / Home & Life / Mobile / broadband) and 4 of 12 do not disclose it: a measurement-error-ridden variable on ~10 points
effect: Exploratory: +/-0.1 slope per unit, t -0.1 on 9 firms; Nordic 0.60 is outside the peer range 0.09-0.44 (extrapolation)

decision: Each peer's slope regressed on distribution share (WLS, weights 1/(se^2+tau_resid^2), residual tau by DerSimonian-Laird for meta-regression); Nordic's slope PREDICTED from its characteristics with a prediction interval that includes tau; Nordic never enters the fit
alternatives_considered: Free Nordic slope; unweighted regression
reason: Makes 'Nordic is different' a testable statement about an observable characteristic rather than a free parameter
effect: Nordic-like (11): +0.18 per unit share (t 0.1); Nordic predicted +0.20 (90% PI -0.39 to +0.78) vs its own +3.41; the 6-firm -2.78 did not survive (P45)

decision: Add the 2008-09 cycle only (guides for 2008Q3-2010Q4); 2001-02 is not attempted
alternatives_considered: 2001-02 and 2008-09; other industries
reason: The industry factor (Microchip distributor days) starts in the June-2008 10-Q and 8-K earnings releases start in 2003-04: 2001-02 has neither the factor nor filed guides. A different industry would add a different mechanism, not an independent test of this one

decision: Actual = the release's own figure only when the narrative sentence equals an income-statement revenue row (0.5%); XBRL first-reported wherever it exists; quarters with no numeric guide are listed, never imputed
alternatives_considered: Narrative figure alone; use Microchip's 'internal planning' figure when it withdrew guidance
reason: Single regex hits caught an outlook row (onsemi 'Revenue $570 to $585') and a comparative (TI $2.88bn); an internal plan is not guidance

decision: Windows dated by the cycle before the result (2008-10, 2011-19, 2020-26, plus Nordic's own quarters); one fixed sd of the factor for all windows and Nordic
alternatives_considered: Expanding z (as in the forecast); windows chosen to maximise contrast
reason: A descriptive stability test needs one scale to compare slopes; the forecast keeps the point-in-time z

decision: Quarter-level regression with the se scaled for the factor's autocorrelation (Bartlett n_eff) is the headline; pooled with quarter-clustered SE is shown next to it
alternatives_considered: Pooled firm-quarter OLS
reason: The factor is common to all firms and autocorrelated (rho 0.65 in Nordic's window): 236 firm-quarters hold ~4 independent observations
effect: peers' slope in Nordic's window +0.69, t 1.5 not 3.3

decision: Treat the beat as management's forecast error: candidate predictors describe how the guide was set (relative optimism, guided growth, guide width, last beat), not only the channel
alternatives_considered: Add more channel factors
reason: The four channel factors correlate 0.72-0.91 on Nordic (one cycle read four ways); peers' revenue YoY sd 29% vs beat sd 3.6% shows guidance absorbs the cycle

decision: guided q/q minus the median guided q/q of the OTHER peers for the same quarter (>= 5 peers), guides released before the quarter ends
alternatives_considered: vs consensus (not public); vs all peers incl. self
reason: point in time; leave-one-out so a firm is not compared with itself

decision: Primary = raw relative optimism; the planned seasonal version (minus last year's same-quarter q/q) kept as robustness
alternatives_considered: Keep the planned seasonal version as primary
reason: For a firm in a deep cycle last year's q/q is the cycle, not seasonality (Nordic 2025Q2 norm +71.7%). Changed AFTER seeing the data: a researcher degree of freedom, disclosed (P55); both versions give t < 1

topic: test on the panel, not on Nordic
decision: The headline test of relative optimism is the 12-peer panel 2008-2026 with walk-forward OOS R2; Nordic fits are shown with and without the 2023Q3-Q4 episode
alternatives_considered: Fit on Nordic's 21 quarters
reason: Nordic holds ~4 independent observations; the panel holds 70 quarters of firm-specific variation (relative optimism is not a common factor)

decision: Stop adding Nordic factors; record the count tried (~12 on 21 quarters)
alternatives_considered: Keep searching until one works
reason: With ~4 independent observations, one 'significant' factor among a dozen is expected by chance; the panel tests are negative
effect: no factor added to the forecast

topic: where the channel is tested next
decision: Test the channel factor on revenue ONE QUARTER PAST THE GUIDE (g2 = actual t+1 / guide t) on the peer panel, walk-forward
alternatives_considered: Keep the Nordic-only h=2 result as the evidence for K1's 'so what'
reason: K1 implies the channel can only matter beyond the guide; one company's result is not enough to put that on the dashboard
effect: OOS R2 +1.7% vs seasonal, t 1.9, 86% of the gain from three quarters

decision: Benchmark = firm's mean past g2 for the same quarter of the year (>= 2 past years); flat (g2 = 0) shown too
alternatives_considered: Last year's same quarter only
reason: Last year alone carries the cycle (P55)

decision: At origin T the slope is trained on rows with quarter <= T-2 (their target T-1 is reported by the end of T)
alternatives_considered: Train on quarter <= T-1
reason: The target of row T-1 is quarter T, not yet reported at the origin: look-ahead

decision: Run the composite a second time with Logitech sell-through acceleration replaced by the acceleration of graph demand (sell-out proxy through the step-5 lag kernel, graph as of the forecast date, h=1); pre-register its Q3 2026 forecast as a challenger; never adopt it on its back-test
alternatives_considered: Add the graph factor as a fifth factor; put it straight into the forecast; leave the graph only in the h=2 model GR
reason: Analyst request 2026-09-26: at least one forecast of the guided quarter should use the graph, so a change to a graph lag or share visibly moves a Q3 number. Swapping one factor keeps the model at two parameters. Added after the factor search was stopped (B40), so only a pre-registered print can test it
effect: Walk-forward beat RMSE 3.41 pts vs 3.35 for the primary and 4.66 for the benchmark (11 quarters); the two composites correlate 0.998 (3 of 4 factors shared), so the back-test cannot tell them apart. Q3 2026: beat +3.8%, USD 238.7m (primary +4.3%, USD 239.8m)

topic: graph-driven forecast one quarter past the guide (step 7b)
decision: Add a Nordic Q4 2026 line (h=2) with GR as the point and GRg (GR with the unreported demand quarter read from Logitech's own guide) as a lag-sensitive challenger; band from the h=2 walk-forward RMSE and the graph's low/high scenario; edge lags editable in the results page's Assumptions tab
alternatives_considered: Put the graph into the guided Q3 points; make GRg the point; leave the graph in the back-test only
reason: Analyst request 2026-09-26: a changed edge lag must visibly re-populate a forecast. The back-test puts the chain's value at h=2 (GR 0.59x the benchmark's error, n 9). But GR fills the unreported quarter by persistence, so a lag that only shifts kernel weight between lags 1 and 2 cannot move it (P74); GRg can, but Logitech guides quarterly only since 2025Q2, so it differs from GR on 4 back-test quarters (2 better, 2 worse) - not enough to promote it
effect: Q4 2026: GR 223 (187-259), GRg 216 (180-253); graph low/high scenario moves GRg ~10m and GR <1m

decision: Screen 10 candidate series x 2 training windows (20 specifications) as one-factor walk-forward regressions of Logitech sales YoY, BEFORE fixing any specification (analyst request); adopt none
alternatives_considered: Fix 3 factors in config first and test once (the pre-registration route)
reason: Analyst chose to look first. The count of specifications is logged so the look is disclosed; any specification fixed after this can only be tested on later prints
effect: No series beats the naive 'same growth as last quarter' forecast out of sample (best: TD Synnex inventory-days change, +0.13, wrong sign); on the 5 guided quarters every series loses to the guide (guide RMSE 1.8 pts vs 2.2-21). Full-sample correlations are high (PC shipments 0.89, Best Buy computing 0.86) because 2021-23 boom and bust dominates; the level relation breaks after 2024 (Logitech +6-7% while PCs -5% in 2026Q2). Logitech forecast stays guide x (1 + beat)
